smallAudienceConclusion: 100 unique valid reveal entries across ten rounds plus ten settlements completed in 672 modeled seconds at 250 ms per RPC, with no missing entries. This is a useful two-entry-per-person reference for 50 people, not a bound on the unlimited entries that those people may submit.
largeLoadConclusion: At 32 ms modeled RPC, all 1000 valid entries opened; a second scenario also tolerated 1000 malformed entries, two RPC outages, 32 ambiguous accepts and 21 journal/index reopens. At 250 ms only 589 of 1000 valid entries opened before the one-hour deadline; 411 were excluded. All rounds settled and indexed queues drained.
modelLimitations: Real production keeper/index/journal, unique timelock ciphertexts and disposable signatures; virtual RPC, blocks and inclusion, with a historical signed beacon.
Constant per-request delay is charged serially, including reads that the production code can overlap. This is a conservative timing budget, not an accurate parallel network scheduler.
Initial transaction inclusion is optimistic at the next modeled block. Actual network congestion, drand outages, estimateGas latency and RPC rate limits are not established by this model.
Model paid entries represent repeated bets from one wallet across ten rounds. The local EVM separately verifies four 50-NFT holder batches and multiple paid wallets.
No mainnet throughput or launch authorization is implied. Release guard and outstanding source/operational checks remain unchanged.
